_comment: Human-curated corrections, kept OUT of the scrapers so the line between what
Snow Peak published and what a person decided stays visible. build_catalog.py
applies these last and stamps span_source='curated'.
Every entry needs a `reason`. If a reason cannot be written, the part stays
unresolved -- an honest gap beats a confident guess.

XCK-128-01.title_en: Multi Function Table Rail Joint (2-piece set)
XCK-128-01.reason: The rail joint. Two come in the box with a bamboo corner, and it is sold on its own as a spare part. It is in NONE of the six IGT collections and its JP category is not IGT, so both halves of the universe miss it -- a catalog built from the vendor's taxonomy has holes exactly where the taxonomy has them. CK-119TR's manual, step 4: 'レールジョイントを使用する場合はIGTフレームの長辺のレールに挿入します' -- insert them into the rail on the frame's LONG SIDE -- then (5) hook the tabletop onto them. This is what makes the frame's long side attachable at all, and no product page or photograph says it exists.

ST-051.reason: The optional 1-Unit bridge for the Jikaro (ST-050). It lays across the compact (short-edge-in, 365mm) opening to make ONE IGT unit-slot. Like the connection hook and rail joint it cannot exist on its own -- it modifies the Jikaro -- so the planner never places it as its own node; it is a toggle on a Jikaro and its SKU rides that Jikaro's bill. Official Snow Peak SKU (sits next to ST-050), now rare. role 'bridge' is picked up by no palette. See layout.bridges.

CPL-JT2U.reason: The optional 2-Unit bridge for the Jikaro (ST-050): two stainless brackets over the spread (long-edge-in, 600mm) opening + two slide-in bars, making a 2-Unit IGT bay. A toggle on the Jikaro, not its own node (cannot stand alone). The official version is a SEPPOUSAI (Snow Peak Festival) 2023 Autumn limited edition; CPL-JT2U is the after-market equivalent. role 'bridge' is picked up by no palette. See layout.bridges.

LV-077GY.reason: First NON-IGT prop: the Snow Peak Folding Chair (director's chair). A free-standing piece placed AROUND the layout -- it does not connect to the IGT grid, occupies no slot, joins no assembly. role 'seating' -> a 'prop' node: draggable, rotatable, billed, nothing else. 566x594x838mm, 457mm seat; BLACK aluminium X-frame + taupe polyester-canvas seat/back/armrests. Modelled from the LV-077GY photo.

LV-077RD.reason: Red variant of the Folding Chair. Same director's-chair frame and dimensions as LV-077GY, but a SILVER bare-aluminium frame (the gray/mesh ones are black-coated) and a deep-crimson canvas (0x962436, sampled from the LV-077RD photo).

LV-077M-BK.reason: Mesh variant: the same folding director's-chair frame (black), but the seat/back/armrests are a SEE-THROUGH black polyester MESH -- modelled as a dark fabric with a perforated alphaMap (tex/chair_mesh.png). Same 566x594x838 / 457mm seat as LV-077.

LV-091.reason: Low Beach Chair (LV-091KH): a low, reclined beach chair -- SILVER aluminium tube frame, khaki canvas sling (seat + high reclined back, 0xc6b487 sampled from the photo), two STRAIGHT laminated-bamboo armrests. Low 300mm seat, 650x580x860. A prop like the folding chair; chair type 'lowbeach'.

LV-093.reason: Luxury Low Beach Chair (LV-093GY): same low-beach form as LV-091 but a LOWER back (owner's note), a BLACK-coated frame (not silver), and a gray-taupe canvas (0x6e5b54 sampled). Reuses the lowbeach builder -- the lower back falls out of the smaller h (640 vs 860). Wood armrests. Dims ~600x600x640 / 260mm seat are estimated off the photo (Snow Peak publishes no clean US spec).

SET-200.reason: Campfield Futon (SET-200) in its BASIC SOFA form only (owner: the set reconfigures many ways -- bed / chairs / shelves -- but we model just the sofa). A low two-seat loveseat: silver aluminium X-frame base, two taupe seat + two reclined back cushions (0xa08d80 sampled), natural-wood armrests on the ends. chair type 'sofa'; ~1494x749x650. A prop like the chairs.

TM-096OR.reason: Lounge Cushion (TM-096OR): a ROUND cotton-canvas floor cushion, modelled in its FOLDED half-circle seating form (fold the round pad in half -> a half-disc of doubled thickness), as the product photos show. Brick-orange. Open pad ~495mm diameter x 50mm; folded ~495x247x100. chair type 'cushion'; a floor prop, no frame.

TM-096GR.reason: Lounge Cushion (TM-096GR): the olive-green variant of TM-096OR. Same round-folded-to-half-circle floor cushion; olive canvas.

LV-071GY.reason: Folding Bench (LV-071GY): the folding chair's bench sibling -- BACKLESS, armless, a long taupe canvas sling on two black end X-frames tied by a lengthwise stretcher. 1095x330x358 (seat height, no back). chair type 'bench'.

LV-071RD.reason: Folding Bench (LV-071RD): red variant -- SILVER frame + crimson canvas, matching the red folding chair (LV-077RD). Now discontinued but still built per owner. Same bench form as LV-071GY.

LV-071M-BK.reason: Mesh Folding Bench (LV-071M-BK): black frame + see-through black mesh sling (perforated alphaMap), the bench version of the mesh folding chair. Same bench form.

LV-066TR.reason: Bamboo Folding Bench / Shelf Long (LV-066TR): a rigid laminated-bamboo top on folding stainless end X-frames -- a multi-use narrow table / bench / storage shelf. 1095x330x394. chair type 'shelf'; the bamboo top wears the real bamboo grain.

LV-065TR.reason: Bamboo Folding Bench / Shelf, regular (LV-065TR): the shorter sibling of LV-066TR, same bamboo-top-on-folding-X-legs form. Reuses the shelf builder. Dims ~590x300x340 are ESTIMATED (no clean US spec found) -- shorter than the Long.

LV-085.reason: Take! Bamboo Chair (LV-085): the signature Snow Peak chair -- natural BAMBOO X-legs, a slim aluminium seat frame + back posts, a draped cream cotton-canvas seat & back. The hard one (curves approximated with straight tubes). 549x630x749, ~330 seat. chair type 'take'.

GF-051.reason: Takibi Garden Table (ガーデン焚火テーブル L). Excluded from the layout system: it is fixed garden furniture, assembled in place and not meant to be carried or moved, so it does not belong in a planner for a portable kit. The IGT/Layout System is defined by being packable and re-configurable on site; this is not. It stays in the catalog, flagged, because it is a real product and its connection to IGT is real -- just out of scope.

GF-052.reason: Takibi Garden Table XL (ガーデン焚火テーブル LL). Same as GF-051 -- fixed garden furniture, not portable. Excluded from the layout system, kept in the catalog.

GF-015.reason: Garden Unit Table Set (ガーデンユニットテーブル ウッドトップセット). The Garden Unit Table is a stationary garden piece, not part of the movable IGT kit. Excluded from the layout system, kept in the catalog. Its wood insert GF-010 is excluded with it.

GF-010.reason: Garden Unit Table Wood Insert -- the top for GF-015, which is fixed garden furniture. Excluded with its table. (It had been pulled into make_textures as a flat board via FLAT_EXTRA; that is removed too -- it is not an IGT slot insert.)

BG-031.reason: Waterproof Gear Box 1 Unit. NOT a slot insert -- it is a box that HOLDS a unit's worth of gear, and is naturally bigger than a unit all round, so it cannot itself drop into the frame. The US store's '1 Unit' is its CAPACITY (what it holds), not its footprint, and filing it as a slot_module was reading the name as a size. Two tells confirm it: the JP spec is prefixed 内寸 (INNER dimensions) -- 370x260x270 is the CAVITY, the outer shell is larger -- and 370x260 does not even match the slot pattern (250 along-rail x 360 rail-span); it is wider AND shallower. So: role storage, no span, dims flagged as internal. Owner's correction, 2026-07-14.

BG-032.reason: Waterproof Gear Box 2 Unit. Same as BG-031 -- a storage box that holds TWO units, 内寸 (inner) 530x370x270, bigger than a 2-unit footprint (500x360) in both directions. Not a slot insert; the '2 Unit' is capacity, not size.

UG-472.reason: Waterproof Unit Gear Bag 220. THIS is a real slot insert (with UG-471) -- a bag that drops into ONE unit slot. Its dimensions were missing because the JP source has a typo: '（H）220×（W）360×（W）250mm' labels the third axis （W） instead of （D）, and the parser could not read two widths. It is 360 (rail span) x 250 (along-rail = 1 unit) x 220 tall -- the SAME 1-unit footprint as UG-471, just deeper (the '220' is the height code, not a unit count). Span stays 2 (one unit). Owner confirmed UG-471/UG-472 are the units that actually embed.

CK-220.reason: IGT Hanging Rack Frame, 2-tier set (IGTハンギングラックフレーム 2段セット). Two SIDE FRAMES hook over the frame's rails (rotate on, per the manual), and two MAIN FRAMES clip between them at two heights -- so it hangs a 2U-wide two-tier open rack BELOW the frame, adding 2U of shelf on each tier. It occupies 2U of the grid (span 4) and, per the manual, only ONE fits per frame: 'IGTフレーム内に2つ設置できません。サイドフレームが干渉し組み立てが不可能です' -- the side frames collide. Load: 20kg per main frame, 60kg total. DIMS: Snow Peak publishes only the PACKED size (539x368x55); there is no assembled dimension. The 510x354 footprint is taken from its sibling CK-230 (same frame family, 2U wide), and the 372mm drop is MODELLED from the packed side-frame height, not measured. Flagged assembled_estimated.

CK-230.reason: Shallow IGT Hanging Shelf (IGTハンギングラック 浅型). Two side panels open to 90 degrees and four hooks rest OVER the frame's rails (manual: 'フックがテーブル側のレール部に確実に載っている'), hanging a single shelf 242mm below. Unlike CK-220 it brings its OWN surface -- set contents are 本体x1 + unitx1, a base plate (ベースプレート) -- so it is a hanging shelf, not an open rack that holds trays. Assembled 510x354x242 is PUBLISHED (unlike CK-220). Occupies 2U (span 4); load 5kg; ONE per frame -- the manual: 'CK-150...に2台設置できません。製品同士が干渉しますので、1フレームに対し、本製品1つのみ設置してください'.

GP-040.reason: IGT LI Stove Joint Frame (IGT剛炎ジョイントフレーム). Owner: it is 1.5 units (span 3) and its ONLY use is with the GS-1000 (剛炎) stove -- it is the frame that drops that specific burner into the grid. This resolves the one part the catalog had left UNRESOLVED: its along-rail dimension is 362mm = 2.90 half-units, which sits between 1 and 1.5 units and could not be called from millimetres alone. The unit label decides it, as it always does: 1.5U. Its 362mm being 14mm under 375 is the same rim-clearance slack the other cooktops show.

CK-020.reason: IGT Box Hanger, half unit (ステンボックスハンガー ハーフユニット). It hooks onto the frame's END on wire hooks -- the same end-piece holes the bamboo extensions use -- but it is a HANGER, not a tabletop: instead of extending the surface it carries the Stainless Box Half Unit (CK-025) below the outboard edge. JP a001 shows exactly this: two wire hooks in the frame's black end piece, the stainless box hanging off the outside. Owner: its only job is to mount CK-025, though it works empty too (a rag, tools). So CK-025 -- normally a slot-in module (125x360) -- can instead HANG from the frame's end via CK-020. NOT modelled as a placeable node in the planner: it is a peripheral hanger, not a layout surface, and rendering a box-below-the-edge is more than its role in a LAYOUT tool earns. The relationship is recorded; the geometry is deferred.

CK-025.reason: Stainless Box Half Unit. Its default home is a half-unit slot in the frame (attach slot_in, 125x360 = one half-unit x the rail span). But it has a second home: hung off the frame's END by the CK-020 Box Hanger, out of the grid entirely. Two ways to carry the same box, and the planner should not pretend the slot is the only one. It COMES WITH its lid: the JP set contents are リッドトレー、コンテナ (lid tray + container), and the lid tray is CK-026 -- so CK-025 contains CK-026, which is also sold on its own.

CK-026.reason: リッドトレー ハーフユニット -- the LID of the CK-025 box, not a generic 'tray' as the English name reads. A thin (15mm) stainless plate, half-unit, with a finger hole. It ships with CK-025 and is also sold separately. Being a flat plate seen from above, its real photographed surface is textured (the finger hole and logo show), rather than drawn as a blank slab.

attaches_to: any flat tabletop of similar thickness
DB-005.reason: Garbage Frame (ガビングフレーム) -- a spring-wire frame that CLAMPS OVER a flat tabletop EDGE and holds a bin bag open below it. JP a001 shows it gripping the edge of a bamboo top, bag hanging. Owner: it clamps ANYWHERE along a bamboo tabletop edge (or any table of similar thickness), but NOT on an IGT frame -- the frame's edge is rail and modules, not a flat board, so there is nothing to clamp and it would foul the unit. A free-position edge clamp, not a grid part. Owner flagged it as non-core and skippable; recorded here for completeness, not built into the planner.

CK-175.reason: IGTコネクションフック -- what joins two frames END TO END. A frame's end already has the HOLES (measured on CK-149: x = +/-406.5, z = +/-143.9); CK-175 supplies the other half by turning the neighbouring end into a HOOK. It is JP-only, has no manual, and exactly ONE real photograph in its gallery -- which happens to be of exactly this: two frames butted end to end, black end pieces face to face, two knurled thumbscrews spanning the joint, and TWO PAIRS OF LEGS bunched at it (so the frames do not share legs; each keeps its own four). The JP spec table says セット内容 本体×2 and 45g(本体一つあたり) -- a pair, 45g EACH -- so one set makes one joint (one hook per hole) and the SET weighs 90g. The scraper took the 45 as the item weight, which is what the page literally says and is not what it means.

CK-218.reason: ATTACH: the copy never says how the angle extensions attach, and their plan view shows the hooks only if you look for them on the SLANTED edge -- which the detector could not, because it tested for protrusion past the BOUNDING BOX. Two sources settle it. LV-381's manual, in English: 'it is possible to connect this product with a Bamboo IGT Table Regular / Long, Bamboo Left/Right Angle Extension, Bamboo Left / Right Corner Extension (CK-117TR, CK-218, CK-219, CK-118TR, CK-119TR)'. And the owner pointed at the hooks in the top view and at the close-up (JP a009): the same stainless wire hook, let into a slot in the board's edge, arching out and bending straight down. DEPTH: Snow Peak publishes 990x496, but that aspect (1.996) contradicts its own photograph (2.13) by 7% -- on BOTH mirror products, from two independent shots, while CK-117TR and CK-119TR agree with theirs to 0.6% and 0.3%. The hook spacing settles which number is wrong: it must match the frame's end holes (287.8mm), and it is 288-292mm on every other bamboo board. At the published scale CK-218's hooks come out 304mm apart -- a 5% outlier that would not enter the holes. At 990x465 they come out 289mm, the scale is isotropic (1.3866 vs 1.3881 mm/px), and the published WIDTH is reproduced to 0.4%. So 990 is real and 496 is not the bounding box; what Snow Peak means by it, I do not know, and am not going to invent. This matters because the ANGLE is measured in this frame: at the published scale the leg reads 61.2deg (turn 57.6), and at the true one 59.7deg (TURN 60.0).

CK-219.reason: Mirror of CK-218; same evidence and the same 6.4% aspect discrepancy in its own photograph, independently shot. Measured turn: 60.6deg.

GS-450R.reason: Along-rail 270mm against a 250mm unit. The extra 20mm is the rim resting on the rails, the way any drop-in cooktop overlaps its cutout -- the burner body drops through one unit. Snow Peak's own copy says only 'compatible with the Iron Grill Table System' and never states a count.

GS-230.reason: Along-rail 563mm against two units (500mm), same rim logic as GS-450R. Corroborated by the product copy: 'Pair the Double Burner Stove with the IGT 4 Unit Standing Set and the Double Bamboo Insert' -- the double insert takes 2 units, so the stove takes the remaining 2.

S-029HA.reason: Not an IGT part. It is a Takibi Fire & Grill accessory that the US storefront files under `cookers`. Its 'half-unit size' copy refers to the Takibi grill, not an IGT unit -- measured along-rail is 206mm against a 125mm half unit, which the fit cross-check flagged at +81mm.

S-029HD.reason: Same as S-029HA. Its own description says 'Use the Grill Plate Half Deep Depth within the Takibi Fire & Grill'.

GS-1000.reason: Round stove (JP size is written as a diameter, φ350x420). It does not sit in the grid on its own -- it mounts via the GP-040 joint frame, which is the part that occupies units.

CK-090.reason: Not an extension piece — it is a table in its own right. The copy: 'The Extension IGT is a two-unit expandable Iron Grill Table... does not require any connection tools or extension pieces... two laminated bamboo tabletops and an aluminum alloy stand.' JP size gives it away too: 1348×498×400(h)mm at 11kg, with its own legs. It stands at 400mm — the Layout System datum — so it joins the system as a node, not as a part bolted to a frame.

_GP-040_note: GP-040 is resolved above (span 3, 1.5U, GS-1000-only). It was UNRESOLVED for weeks -- 362x377mm is neither 250 nor 375 cleanly, and no published number decides it -- until the owner supplied the unit label. The label always wins over millimetres; this was the last part waiting on one.
